articles.title: CWRC directs Karnataka to release 2,000 cusecs of Cauvery water daily to Tamil Nadu for 15 days
articles.summary: New Delhi: The Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) on Friday directed Karnataka to release 2,000 cusecs of Cauvery water every day for the next 15 days, beginning 8 am on November 20, to ensure the stipulated flows reach Billigundlu. The committee, chaired by Vineet Gupta, reviewed the crop situation, rainfall patterns and reservoir storage across the Cauvery basin before issuing the order. Under the directive, Karnataka must release a total of 2.76 thousand million cubic feet (tmc ft) of water to Tamil Nadu during the period. Karnataka informed the committee that inflows into its four major Cauvery reservoirs were 53.88 per cent below the 30-year average. Drought conditions had affected 55 of the 56 taluks in the state’s Cauvery basin, it said. Supreme Court dismisses Tamil Nadu's pleas on release of Cauvery water The state also noted that rainfall below Mettur was 23 per cent above normal and that Tamil Nadu’s Mettur, Bhavani and Amaravathy reservoirs together held 37.125 tmcft as on November 5. Karnataka argued that Tamil Nadu could meet its Samba irrigation requirements until December 15 with existing storage, monsoon flows and groundwater. Of the projected 57 tmc ft available to Karnataka, 50 tmc ft would be required to meet priority needs until the end of July 2027, leaving only 7 tmc ft—insufficient for standing crops. The state therefore requested that no further releases be ordered from its reservoirs. Tamil Nadu, meanwhile, demanded clearance of a backlog of 16.895 tmc ft. It urged the committee to assess pro-rata shares based on observed inflows, releases and water use across the basin states, and to factor in Karnataka’s withdrawals for minor irrigation, lift irrigation and tank filling.

Emphasising that no individual was above the organisation, Bansal told leaders not to indulge in any conduct that could compel the party to initiate disciplinary proceedings against them. "Do not act in a manner that leaves the party with no option but to take disciplinary action against you," he told the gathering, according to party sources. The meeting was attended by state BJP president Samik Bhattacharya, district presidents, divisional in-charges and other organisational functionaries. The BJP, which secured a resounding mandate in assembly elections and formed the government under Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, has since been grappling with the organisational challenges accompanying its transition from the opposition to the ruling establishment. Despite those reservations, former TMC functionaries have continued to join the BJP in different districts, with some of the inductions allegedly taking place with the backing of local party leaders. The developments have reportedly triggered resentment among sections of the BJP's old guard, with rival groups questioning the manner in which new entrants are being accommodated. The issue has increasingly become a source of internal friction, with the leadership facing the challenge of balancing political expansion with the concerns of cadres who worked for the party during its years in opposition. Bansal's intervention is being seen as an attempt by the central leadership to reinforce organisational authority at a time when the BJP is consolidating its position as the ruling party in West Bengal. articles.title: Bike taxi drivers, ride aggregators push for clear regulations after SC verdict
articles.summary: Bengaluru: With the Supreme Court upholding the Karnataka High Court's order allowing bike taxis to operate in the state, drivers, aggregator platforms and commuters have urged the government to expedite the framing of a clear regulatory framework to ensure the service can function without uncertainty and harassment. While the verdict has brought relief to thousands of bike taxi drivers who have faced disruptions to their livelihoods, stakeholders say the absence of specific regulations continues to leave them vulnerable on city roads. Drivers allege they are frequently confronted by auto and cab drivers, who question their right to operate and threaten consequences for providing what is often labelled an "illegal" service. Rapido rider stabbed to death after drinking session in Bengaluru's Koramangala "In the past four years, I've completed 25,000 rides. Dropped all passengers safely. But still, my job lacks credibility. Especially in the last few months, I've been confronted with rowdy auto and cab drivers who harass not just me, but also passengers. This deters passengers," said Nanjundan K, a 59-year-old bike taxi driver hoping government regulations will help curb the on-ground harassment. Drivers said the uncertainty had also affected their ability to work consistently, with some reporting confrontations while picking up or dropping off passengers. They said formal recognition and a defined set of rules would help distinguish legitimate operators from those violating regulations. "Now, that the legal position has been clarified, the next step should be for the government to put regulations in place. A structured framework will benefit drivers, platforms and commuters, while ensuring that passenger safety is not compromised. From our end, we'll do our best to push the government towards forming the new rules at the earliest," said Adi Narayan, president of the Bike Taxi Welfare Association of Karnataka. The regulations would also help ensure uniform fares across aggregator platforms, stated Mohammed Salim, president of Namma Bike Taxi Association. A failed bank payment, a stranded passenger — and a suspected bike taxi scam in Bengaluru "Currently, while the base fare across platforms is around Rs 25-35, the per km fare differs. While Rapido offers Rs 7/km, Uber and Ola offer around Rs 10-11/km. Plus, unlike autos, we don't get paid extra for night duty. All this needs to be taken into consideration while forming the bike taxi rules. Plus, there needs to be an emphasis on job security," he added. Pavan Guntupalli, Co-founder, Rapido, which pioneered bike taxi services in Bengaluru, said a clear, practical and progressive regulatory framework is the way forward. "We encourage the Karnataka government to focus on four key aspects while framing the policy: uniform safety and insurance standards across operators; simple, transparent and time-bound digital processes for registration and licensing; integration of bike taxis with the wider public transport ecosystem to strengthen last-mile connectivity; and consultations with commuters, women riders, Captains and operators to ensure the framework addresses ground realities,” he said. An Uber spokesperson said, "The decision brings much-needed regulatory clarity and recognises bike taxis as an important mobility option, offering commuters an affordable and convenient way to navigate congested cities while creating flexible earning opportunities for drivers.”

articles.title: AP raises semiconductor incentives, offers up to 80% support for silicon fabs
articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government has amended its Semiconductor and Display Fab Policy 4.0 to align it with the second phase of the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM 2.0), offering state incentives that match Union support for several project categories. The amendment, notified through G.O.Ms.No.87 on November 16, provides combined Union and State incentives of up to 80% of eligible capital costs for silicon fabrication projects, with each government contributing 40%. Compound semiconductor, photonics, sensor, discrete semiconductor and display fabrication projects, as well as advanced packaging units, will be eligible for combined support of up to 70%. Legacy packaging units can receive up to 50%, according to the policy details. For assembly, testing, marking and packaging (ATMP) and outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) facilities, Andhra Pradesh will match 100% of the Centre’s capital support. The state will also provide a deployment-linked incentive of 4.5% of net sales, in addition to the Union’s 9%, taking the combined incentive to 13.5%. This support will be capped at Rs 45 crore per application and Rs 180 crore per company. For semiconductor machinery and materials projects, the state will provide 18% of eligible capital costs on top of the Union’s 30%, bringing the combined support to 48%, in addition to the Union’s production-linked incentive. Research and development and talent projects will receive state support of 25% of eligible project costs, with combined Union and State assistance capped at 75%. IT Minister Nara Lokesh said the amended policy covers all 10 categories under ISM 2.0, across six pillars: design, machinery and materials, fabrication, packaging, research and development, and talent. The state is also planning a 5,000-acre AP Semiconductor Park in Tirupati to host manufacturers and suppliers across the value chain. The proposed park would provide developed land, shared cleanrooms, reliable high-voltage power, ultrapure water, gas supplies, effluent treatment and recycling, testing laboratories, logistics facilities, and research and training centres. A public-private company with an investor-led board would operate the park, with up to three government nominees. The government also plans to establish an AP Semiconductor Growth and Innovation Council as a single point of contact for investors, alongside an Oversight Council chaired by the Chief Minister and a CEO-led Apex Committee. The AP Semiconductor Research and Innovation Centre is proposed as a not-for-profit organisation with independent professional management. It will initially operate at IIT Tirupati before moving to the park, with photonics as its first area of focus. The amended policy will remain in force for five years or until it is replaced by a new policy. Existing benefits will be protected, while separate operating guidelines will set out eligibility, appraisal and disbursement procedures.

articles.title: UoH students launch protest seeking professor’s termination over casteist remarks
articles.summary: University of Hyderabad students have launched an indefinite protest demanding the termination of Dr Vijaya Ramdas Mandala, a faculty member in the History Department, over his alleged derogatory remarks about Dalit students in an email exchange. The remarks were allegedly made after a former student expressed hesitation regarding incorporating certain suggestions made by Vijaya Ramdas into his research because of ethical concerns. The incident took place in April but came to light only recently. The protest has been called by the Students’ Union, which comprises various student groups, including the Students’ Federation of India (SFI), the Ambedkar Students’ Association, the Dalit Students’ Union,and the Tribal Students’ Forum. Students have been staging a sit-in outside the Social Sciences building, demanding Vijaya Ramdas’s termination. “We will not call off the protest until Vijaya Ramdas is terminated,” Students’ Union general secretary Aditya Rao told TNM. “We had protested earlier too, but no concrete action was taken against him,” he added. In an email exchange accessed by TNM, Vijaya Ramdas contacted Sandeep (name changed), who is a PhD student at Manchester Business School, about corrections to his chapter for a forthcoming book by Bloomsbury India. In the email thread, the History professor refers to former students from the Dalit community as “untouchables” more than once. He also refers to another student studying at Nottingham as “Dalit untouchable idiot”. The email exchange, which took place between April 14 and 16, grew increasingly tense after Sandeep said he would need the permission of his current university to anonymise the people he was being asked to name in the research, to avoid being flagged for ethical violations. “It will take months to get an ethical review committee's decision from the University of Manchester to write the names asked for in my chapter and publish it as a PhD student of the University,” Sandeep said. Vijaya Ramdas responded: “At Indian business schools, or even at Harvard Business School or Rotman Business School, your chapter discussing managerial and business people would not have been a problem. It's not a History Department perspective, as 99.5% of History departments worldwide do not deal with business history.” Sandeep then pointed to another obstacle in the research, saying that one of the students who is part of his research would need approval to conduct research in India. He also said the researcher was unclear about the archival sources. Vijaya Ramdas responded: “The recent German PhD who comes from an untouchable Dalit background also said to me the same thing about his collection of archives in India.” He further wrote: “A large chunk of the Indian population is from non-Aryan and non-wealthy backgrounds, including backward states like Bihar and Jharkhand, which resemble some countries in Africa on the political map of India and across the globe. This also happened to another Dalit untouchable idiot at Nottingham, who is working part-time in a hotel in England after his post-UK PhD (sic).” Vijaya Ramdas also called Sandeep “anti-Indian”, threatened to withhold academic support, and said his chapter would not be included in the book. He said people from poverty-ridden backgrounds developed “Pakistani-centric thinking (not knowing that one cannot emulate class, one should be born in a high class and culture) in a country known as Mini-Pakistan.” “I am terminating further communication with you, but also will not provide academic support from third-rate, poverty-ridden idiots from Bihar and Jharkhand henceforth,” he concluded. In addition to seeking Vijaya Ramdas’s termination, the students have called for his arrest under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act. They have also demanded that Bloomsbury India suspend its ongoing project with him and that caste sensitisation workshops be held across the University.

articles.title: Karnataka HC quashes case against pharmacy chain MedPlus for collecting an 'extra Rs 1.12'
articles.summary: Bengaluru: The High Court of Karnataka has quashed proceedings against the director and in-charge director of pharmacy retail chain MedPlus for selling seven tablets instead of eight tablets and collecting an excess amount of Rs 1.12. Setting aside the proceedings initiated in 2016, Justice S Vishwajit Shetty observed that such prosecution is an abuse of process of law. Karnataka HC relief for student whose marks card was withheld over phone during scrapped NEET The petitioners, P Srinivas, Director and M Surendranath, the in-charge Director of MedPlus, and others challenged the proceedings pending before a court in Bengaluru for offences under Clause 26 of the Drugs (Price Control) Order, and Section 7(1)(a)(ii) of the Essential Commodities Act. The private complaint was filed by Shrinath Joshi, Senior Reporter, ETV Kannada News, Bengaluru. It stated that on August 23, 2016, he had purchased certain medicines from the outlet in Bengaluru. On August 26, he filed the complaint stating that while the outlet supplied seven tablets of Lanzol Junior 15 mg tablets, the bill was raised for Rs 40.32 for eight tablets and an excess amount of Rs 1.12 was collected from him. The court noted that Clause 26 of the Drugs (Price Control) Order gets attracted only if a person sells any formulation to any consumer at a price exceeding the price specified in the price list or the label of the container or packs thereof, whichever is less. Karnataka HC refuses to quash proceedings against geologist under Prevention of Corruption Act "It is not the case of the prosecution that the accused persons had collected an excess amount than the price indicated on the label of the container or pack thereof, whichever is less. Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that prosecution of the petitioners for the aforesaid offences would not only cause embarrassment to them, but would also amount to abuse of process of law,” the court said.

articles.summary: Hyderabad: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu directed officials to prepare an action plan to transform Andhra Pradesh Mineral Development Corporation (APMDC) into a premier mining organisation on the lines of NMDC. He suggested that the corporation could seek the assistance of private agencies, if necessary, to achieve this objective. Andhra CM Naidu writes to Union minister Shivraj seeking Rs 96.33 crore aid for cyclone-hit horticulture crops During a review meeting on Mines Department at his camp office on Friday, the Chief Minister discussed on identification of new mineral deposits in the State, their efficient utilisation and opportunities for revenue generation. He directed officials to formulate plans to enhance the value of the State's mineral resources and ensure that local resources are utilised within Andhra Pradesh itself. The Chief Minister emphasised that mineral resources should not be viewed merely as a source of revenue, but should be developed into valuable assets for the future. Officials informed the Chief Minister that 582 mineral potential areas had been identified across 74,860 square kilometres in the State and divided into 209 clusters. The Chief Minister approved the proposal to take APMDC to the stock market through an Initial Public Offering (IPO), targeting its listing by December next year. He directed officials to prepare the IPO proposal based on the equity valuation of APMDC. The Chief Minister also approved the establishment of a dedicated Andhra Pradesh Rare Earth Development Corporation (APREDC) for the development and management of rare earth minerals. He said the new corporation should focus on the exploration of rare earth minerals and value addition. He directed officials to implement plans to accelerate mineral exploration and auction processes over the next five years. The meeting also reviewed proposals to extend the deadline for resolving 6,500 pending quarry lease applications and 223 renewal applications. Their disposal is expected to generate approximately Rs. 400 crore in revenue for the government. Officials further informed the Chief Minister that APMDC was participating in auctions for three coal blocks in Odisha and Jharkhand to ensure coal supplies to thermal power plants. The three blocks together have estimated coal reserves of 1,774.6 million tonnes.

articles.summary: New Delhi: India's fertiliser subsidy is likely to overshoot the budgetary allocation by over Rs 1 lakh crore in the current financial year as prices of key raw materials such as ammonia and sulphur have surged due to the West Asia conflict, analysts said. The Centre has earmarked Rs 1.71 lakh crore for fertiliser subsidy in the 2026-27 budget. Around 80 per cent of this budgeted amount is estimated to have been exhausted by mid-November. According to an estimate by ICRA, fertiliser subsidy is likely to hit an all-time high of Rs 2.76 lakh crore in the current fiscal, which will be Rs 1.05 lakh crore higher than the budgetary allocation. “The increase in subsidy is owing to the sharp increase in the prices of key raw materials such as Ammonia and Sulphur following the geopolitical conflict in West Asia as the countries in this region are key suppliers of these commodities," ICRA said. While prices of key fertiliser inputs have moderated from their post-war highs, these still remain significantly higher than pre-war levels. The Union Budget for 2026-27 was presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on February 1, 2026, nearly a month before the outbreak of US-Israel-Iran conflict. The current financial year’s fertiliser subsidy is likely to exceed the previous peak of Rs 2.55 lakh core registered in 2022-23 following the onset of the Russia-Ukraine war. In the financial year ended March 2026 fertiliser subsidy stood at Rs 2.11 lakh crore. The subsidy allocation for Phosphorus and Potassium (P&K) fertilisers has been budgeted at Rs. 0.54 lakh crore for FY2027, while that of urea stands at Rs 1.17 lakh crore. Short-term gains from chemical fertilisers come at cost of our soil and health: N Chaluvarayaswamy The actual expenditure on both these segments is estimated to be sharply higher. ICRA estimates the subsidy requirement for the P&K fertiliser segment to be Rs 1.02 lakh crore for FY2027 against the budgetary allocation of Rs. 0.54 lakh crore. The Union Cabinet recently approved a sharp increase in fertiliser support for the 2026-27 rabi season, lifting the allocation to Rs 62,370 crore. Indian fertiliser manufacturers source a sizable amount of finished products and raw materials from West Asia, including urea, DAP, ammonia and, most notably, sulphur. Post the West Asia crisis, the industry diversified its sourcing base towards alternative geographies though the cost of procurement remains elevated The inventory levels remain healthy for urea and P&K fertilisers owing to proactive procurement by the industry and the Government. After the successful closure of urea import tenders of 2.5 MMT in April 2026 and 1.7 MMT in June 2026, India Potash Ltd issued a tender of 1.7 MMT of which less than 25 per cent of the tendered quantity was filled due to aggressive pricing. Stocks of all major fertilisers are higher on a year-on-year basis as on November 11, 2026. The industry participants have also increased procurement from Russia, North Africa and other regions, ICRA said. “India is likely to remain reliant on imports for meeting incremental requirements, particularly for urea, DAP and key raw materials such as ammonia and sulphur,” it added.

articles.summary: New Delhi: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday said cultural and civilisational cooperation will strengthen relations among various countries and twenty-first-century technology has created new possibilities for cultural connectivity. Inaugurating the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum here, Modi also said that thousands of years of priceless heritage is preserved in the museums, libraries and archives of India, and with the help of technology, this heritage can be passed on to the new generation. PM Modi to inaugurate 'Nitish Setu' over Ganga in Bihar on November 21 "In recent years, the SCO has significantly increased cooperation in security, economy and connectivity. In such a scenario, cultural and civilisational cooperation will further strengthen relations among various countries. "I am confident that new ideas will emerge from this forum, new opportunities for cultural cooperation will be created and our shared civilisational experiences will play a crucial role in uniting the world," he said. The prime minister said empires have certainly changed the maps of the world, but civilisational dialogues have changed the world's ideas and enriched them. "Therefore, the SCO Civilisational Summit is not merely a ceremonial platform but it can become a platform to give direction to the world," he said. Modi said the 21st-century technology has created new possibilities for cultural connectivity in the world. "Across the very routes where our ancestors once had to travel for months, people from those same countries can now connect with one another in just a few seconds. Digital platforms have made knowledge sharing, cultural exchange and international collaboration easier than ever before." "SCO countries should take full advantage of these new possibilities," he said. 'A compromised PM can never sit at this table': Rahul Gandhi takes dig at PM Modi over Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral meet The three-day SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum is being hosted by India at the historic Purana Quila here, and delegates from various SCO member countries, including Pakistan minister Musadik Malik, are attending the event. The two-day event is being hosted by the Ministry of Culture and the Ministry of External Affairs on Friday and Saturday. The SCO was founded at a summit in Shanghai in 2001 by the presidents of Russia, China, the Kyrgyz Republic, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. India and Pakistan became its permanent members in 2017. Iran became a member in 2023.

articles.title: Congress wins big in Rajasthan panchayat elections
articles.summary: Jaipur: The Congress in Rajasthan registered a decisive victory over the ruling BJP in the panchayat elections on Friday and said this is a message by the people to the government's "neglect and unfulfilled promises". The Congress won 3,701 Panchayat Samiti seats against the BJP's 2,181 and 599 Zila Parishad seats against the ruling party's 301, according to the State Election Commission (SEC). It won more Panchayat Samiti seats than the BJP in 33 of the 37 districts where counting was held, while the ruling party finished ahead in only four districts - Ajmer, Balotra, Salumber and Udaipur. The results are a setback to the BJP and come weeks before the government led by Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma completes three years in office in December. According to figures displayed on the SEC website Friday evening, results were available for 7,393 of the 7,543 Panchayat Samiti seats and 981 of the 1,275 Zila Parishad seats across 37 districts. In the Panchayat Samiti elections, Rashtriya Loktantrik Party (RLP) headed by Nagaur MP Hanuman Beniwal won 496 seats, Bharat Adivasi Party (BAP) 276, BSP 60, CPI(M) 50 and AAP two, while Independents secured 627 seats. In the Zila Parishad elections, the RLP won 37 seats, BAP 22, BSP and CPI(M) six each, and Independents 10. The Congress performed strongly in Jaipur, winning 216 Panchayat Samiti seats against the BJP's 87. In Jodhpur, it secured 195 seats against the BJP's 81. 'Bitten by mad dogs'| Revanth Reddy's jibe at dissident party MLAs triggers fresh revolt in Telangana Congress The opposition party also secured 165 seats against the BJP's 111 in Bhilwara, 155 against 65 in Bikaner, 135 against 59 in Dausa and 179 against 87 in Sikar. In Bharatpur, the home district of Chief Minister Sharma, the Congress won 46 Panchayat Samiti seats against the BJP's 32. Independents secured 76 seats. In Deeg, the home district of Minister of State for Home Jawahar Singh Bedham, the Congress won 25 seats against the BJP's 14, while Independents secured 41 seats. In western Rajasthan, the Congress won 120 seats against the BJP's 62 in Barmer, 89 against 36 in Jaisalmer and 97 against 58 in Rajsamand. The BJP, however, finished ahead of the Congress in Ajmer, winning 83 Panchayat Samiti seats against 80, Balotra (63 against 57), Salumber (38 against 32) and Udaipur (146 against 137). In the Zila Parishad elections, the Congress was ahead of the BJP in seat tallies in 24 districts, while the BJP led in six - Ajmer, Beawar, Dungarpur, Jhalawar, Pali and Udaipur, according to district-wise results displayed on the SEC website. In Sikar, Urban Development and Housing Minister Jhabar Singh Kharra's wife Shanti Devi and his two sons lost the Panchayat Samiti elections. Shanti Devi and Ajay Singh contested as BJP candidates from wards 17 and 20, respectively, while Kharra's other son Durga Singh contested as an Independent from ward 19. In Churu, however, senior BJP leader and former minister Rajendra Rathore's son Parakram Singh Rathore and daughter-in-law Kanika Singh won the Zila Parishad elections. Parakram Singh won from ward 39 by a margin of 17,861 votes, while his wife Kanika Singh secured victory from ward 23 by 2,384 votes. Reacting to the results, former chief minister Ashok Gehlot said that rural voters, including farmers, labourers and women, have sent a clear message against the BJP government. PM 'rattled', realised he will soon become 'outgoing PM': Congress on Modi's FICCI address "This is their message to the government's neglect and unfulfilled promises," he said. BJP spokesperson Ram Lal Sharma acknowledged that the party's performance fell short of expectations and said it would review the results, identify shortcomings and take corrective measures ahead of future elections. Counting was held for 7,543 Panchayat Samiti seats and 1,275 Zila Parishad seats across 37 of the state's 41 districts. In the remaining four districts of Kota, Baran, Karauli and Sri Ganganagar, counting has been deferred to December 17 as the five-year terms of the existing Zila Parishads and Panchayat Samitis expire next month. According to the SEC, 4,069 candidates contested 1,275 Zila Parishad wards and 25,108 candidates were in the fray for 7,543 Panchayat Samiti wards across 419 Panchayat Samitis in the 37 districts. Across all 41 districts, the elections covered 1,403 Zila Parishad wards and 8,245 Panchayat Samiti wards in 457 Panchayat Samitis. In the previous Panchayat elections held during 2020-21, the BJP won 1,989 Panchayat Samiti seats against the Congress's 1,852 in 21 districts in December 2020. The Congress subsequently won 678 seats against the BJP's 551 in six districts in September 2021, and 278 against 165 in four districts in December 2021. The number of Zila Parishad seats has since increased from 1,014 to 1,403 and Panchayat Samiti seats from 6,992 to 8,245.

articles.title: Sugarcane price: Savadi seeks lasting fix for farmer-mill price dispute row
articles.summary: Mangaluru: A permanent solution must be found to end the recurring conflicts between sugar factory owners and sugarcane growers every year, said Co-operation Minister Laxman Savadi. Speaking to reporters in Mangaluru on Friday, he highlighted the major demands of farmers, the sugarcane prices announced in Karnataka and neighbouring Maharashtra, and the need for the Union government to take steps to regulate prices. Haveri farmers unite, announce indefinite protest over sugarcane price Savadi said a permanent solution was necessary to prevent farmers from taking to the streets every year. Farmers have put forward three major demands: fixing a fair price for sugarcane, determining the price of sugar and ensuring an appropriate price for ethanol. They have also demanded that the government purchase 100% of the ethanol produced, he said. He said that following recent discussions between farmer leaders and sugar factory owners in Belagavi, an initial price of Rs. 3,300 per tonne had been announced. articles.title: 'Heritage is not just a building': 8.5 lakh books at risk at Central Secretariat Library, SC flags
articles.summary: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Friday said heritage is not confined to structures alone, while voicing deep concern over the fate of nearly 8.5 lakh books in the 135-year-old Central Secretariat Library amid the Central Vista redevelopment. A bench of Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva directed that the suo motu matter be placed before the Chief Justice of India for listing before an appropriate bench. Until then, the Centre’s November 16 undertaking that the books will not be shifted will remain in force. “Heritage is not just a Newton’s bungalow. Is it not? We need to look at these books. One book dates back to the 1700s and something like that. We need to treasure those,” Justice Kumar told the Centre’s counsel. The court pointed to photographs of volumes stored in RK Puram for 15 years and remarked on their condition. The bench recalled the 2009 fire that destroyed the Hyderabad High Court library’s historic collection. “Chief Justice A R Dave cried literally. He had tears in his eyes because we lost those books. That is how much we treasured those books,” Justice Kumar said. Supreme Court seeks Centre’s response on awareness drive against consanguineous marriages Solicitor General Tushar Mehta concurred, invoking the ancient library at Nalanda to underline that such losses are irreversible. “We are conscious and the government is also conscious of the fact,” he said, adding that officers would sit with the amicus to find a workable solution while abiding by the undertaking. The library, housed across four floors of Shastri Bhawan since 1969, faces uncertainty over relocation under the Central Vista project without clear arrangements for the collection’s upkeep. The court had earlier taken suo motu cognisance of media reports on the issue. In October, it sought the actual layout plan and details of space to be allotted for the library. Justice Kumar noted that the subject fell outside the bench’s roster and insisted on following procedure, alluding to recent administrative shifts of cases. Mehta raised no objection to the same bench continuing, but the court preferred the formal course. The books, the court made clear, must not become casualties of redevelopment.

articles.summary: Thiruvananthapuram: From 'Sabun' nut tree, which used to serve the purpose of washing soap, to the non-venomous common wolf snake, that are being widely killed by misinterpreting as highly venomous common krait, seven living things have been declared as official living things by a panchayat in Keralam as part of its efforts to protect biodiversity. The Nochad panchayat on the suburbs of Kozhikode district, which made the official declaration on Thursday, considers it as a first-of-its-type initiative by a local body to protect biodiversity. Keralam becoming a safe destination for students from Manipur The initiative assumes much significance at a time when greeneries are being replaced with concrete structures for development and thereby posing a serious threat to ecology. "It's the understanding about the importance of protecting the ecology that we took the initiative. The species that are facing the threat of getting endangered have been identified with the active participation of the people of the panchayat, ecological experts and those with traditional know-how ," panchayat president Shiji Kottarakkal told DH. The initiative is aimed at making the people aware of the need to protect these living beings. The panchayat has a population of around 24,000 of which majority are farmers. Official living things of Nochad panchayat Flower : 'Tumba', Leucas aspera, is a herb in the mint family. While its white flowers are used for making floral carpets during Onam festival, its leaves and roots are widely used for Ayurvedic medicines. Flower Tumba Tree: 'Sabun nut', Soap nut or wash nut, 'Sapindus emarginatus'. It is believed that this tree got the name as its fruits were widely used for washing purposes during the early years and thus it got the name. Saponins contained in its fruits lather in water and used for cleaning purposes. The tree is now seen only at a couple of spots in the panchayat. Bird: 'Chemban Mullankozhi', Red spurfowl or Galloperdix spadicea, is commonly referred to as forest hen by local people. It is an endangered species in the pheasant family. It is considered to have a secretive nature and it is not easy to spot the bird. Red spurfowl Butterfly: 'Vellilatozhi', Commander or Moduza Procris, is a medium sized butterfly with a wingspan of six to 7.5 centimetres. Commander Dragonfly: 'Tulathumbi', known as Pantala flavescens, the globe skimmer, globe wanderer or wandering glider. People with traditional knowledge used to say that spotting this dragon fly indicates the arrival of a good climate. Wandering glider Fish: 'Manpottan' alias 'Payatti' alias 'Poolan' is known as Tank goby and Glossogobius giuris. It used to be commonly found in paddy fields and other wetlands. This species often remains standstill but will swiftly move away while attempting the catch. Tank goby Snake: 'Vellivarayan', Common wolf snake or Lycodon aulicus. Though it is a non venomous snake it is often misinterpreted as the highly venomous common krait. Hence it is being widely killed and hence facing the threat of getting endangered.

articles.summary: Hyderabad: The removal of senior leader Konda Surekha from the state Cabinet in September may have helped Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy checkmate his critics within the Congress. Months later, however, fresh challenges appear to have emerged, both for him and for the party’s central leadership, which is now being watched for how it will navigate the situation and restore order in the Telangana unit. Telangana CM Revanth Reddy drops Konda Surekha from Cabinet, sends recommendation to Governor In recent weeks, party MLAs Komatireddy Rajagopal Reddy and J Anirudh Reddy have openly voiced dissent, stopping short of naming Revanth Reddy directly. The Chief Minister’s latest remark about them, suggesting they may have been “bitten by mad dogs,” has only reinforced the impression that all is not well in the party. Rajagopal Reddy's elder brother Komatireddy Venkat Reddy is a member of Revanth Reddy's cabinet. 'KTR drove sister out of home, will he do good to people': Telangana CM Revanth Reddy Speaking at a public meeting in Siddipet on Thursday, Revanth Reddy said some dissenting party members seemed to have been “bitten by mad dogs” and that party workers would take them to the Erragadda mental hospital. Though he named no one, the remarks are understood to be aimed at Munugode MLA Rajagopal Reddy and Jadcherla MLA Anirudh Reddy, both of whom have lately been vocal about the Chief Minister’s style of functioning. The turn is notable in Rajagopal Reddy’s case. Days after the Surekha episode, he, who until then had targeted Revanth Reddy now and then, was seen hugging the Chief Minister in a show of unity. Three days ago, however, he launched a scathing attack, questioning Revanth Reddy’s leadership style and the government’s approach to development funding. He warned that a “war will begin” if the Chief Minister believed that being in power entitled him to act as he wish. Objecting to the language used against an elected representative seeking funds for his constituency, Rajagopal Reddy also took a swipe at Revanth Reddy, saying he had become Chief Minister by good fortune. His grouse was that funds for Munugode were not being released on par with Kodangal, the Chief Minister’s own constituency. After the “mad dogs” remark, Rajagopal Reddy posted a cryptic message on social media, widely read as a reference to the Chief Minister alleging wicked administration and rampant corruption. “Leaders holding high office should speak with dignity,” he wrote. “They must realise that people will not applaud those who behave arbitrarily out of arrogance born of power. Rulers who, having gained power by good fortune, indulge in rampant corruption, ignore the needs of the people and run a wicked administration will never be forgiven by the people of Telangana or by history.” “I pray to Lord Ayyappa to bless the key leaders with good sense and the wisdom of self-reflection, so that they implement the promises they have made and govern righteously and honestly,” he added. Anirudh Reddy, meanwhile, has expressed frustration over delays in clearing development bills and questioned the government’s response to pending works in his Jadcherla constituency. He further alleged that officials were demanding commissions from contractors to clear pending bills. Dissent is not confined to these legislators. Peddapalli MP G Vamshi Krishna has publicly questioned Industries Minister D Sridhar Babu over the absence of certain party leaders from a Congress programme in Delhi recently.

articles.title: Kuppam airport clearance puts Tamil Nadu's proposed Hosur airport project in jeopardy
articles.summary: Chennai: With the Union Ministry of Civil Aviation granting stage-1 site clearance for the greenfield Kuppam airport project in Andhra Pradesh ’s Chittoor district, the Tamil Nadu government’s proposal to build an exclusive airport for the burgeoning industrial city of Hosur has hit a major roadblock. The Union Ministry of Defence had, in January this year, refused to allot airspace for the proposed airport in the Hosur–Berigai–Bagalur–Shoolagiri quadrilateral, arguing that it had been reserved for Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) in Bengaluru . Despite the refusal, the then DMK government had written to the Union Government to reconsider the decision, as a 2,000-acre land had already been identified in Krishnagiri district for the ambitious project. After the TVK government took over, Industries Minister S Keerthana had said the airport project will be implemented in a way that does not affect people. However, the stage-1 clearance for building a brand-new airport in Kuppam has made prospects “much more difficult” for Hosur, since the proposed site is barely 70 to 80 km from the chosen quadrilateral. Adding to the hurdles is the Karnataka government’s own proposal to build a second airport for Bengaluru to meet the growing demand of air passengers. The airspace in and around Bengaluru is controlled by HAL for its training operations, making it difficult to allot airspace for additional airports in the region, sources aware of the developments told DH. An airport in Kuppam, strategically located at the tri-junction of Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka, has been a long-cherished dream of Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu, who represents the Kuppam constituency in the Andhra Pradesh Assembly. That TDP’s K Ram Mohan Naidu is the Minister of Civil Aviation made things easy for Andhra Pradesh get the nod for Kuppam airport. Industry sources in Hosur also told DH that Kuppam getting stage-1 clearance makes the chances of an airport in the city “bleak” but wants the state government to push for the project with the Union Government arguing that freight traffic will be huge in Hosur. Another source said the location was chosen with much care, and even the pre-feasibility study by the AAI preferred this quadrilateral not merely because it had fewer obstacles than Belagondapalli, where Taneja owns a private airstrip, but also for its proximity to the Tamil Nadu section of the Satellite Town Ring Road (STRR). The project has encountered several problems ever since the idea was floated — the concrete announcement came in June 2024 by the then Chief Minister M K Stalin — since the concessionaire agreement of the Kempegowda International Airport in Bengaluru says no airport can come up within 150 km radius till 2033. The then Tamil Nadu government did initiate back-channel talks with the Bengaluru International Airport Limited (BIAL) seeking a no-objection certificate for the project.

articles.title: OM review: Dhanush and Mammootty team up for a spy thriller that loses the plot halfway
articles.summary: OM: Operation Mole (Tamil) In 2015, the Andhra Pradesh Red Sanders Anti-Smuggling Task Force opened fire on 20 Tamil labourers in Seshachalam. The cops claimed it was self-defence. The men’s families and human rights organisations have maintained that these were unprovoked extrajudicial murders. At the time, police said they stumbled on the men attempting to cut down red sanders trees for smuggling. But allegations only grew that the so-called ‘encounter’ was staged. No clear answers have emerged since. Their deaths are the heart of Director Rajkumar Periasamy’s OM: Operation Mole. Dhanush plays Palani alias Thirukumaran, a special operative trained in infiltrating organised crime networks. He’s soon sent undercover to a Red Sanders smuggling operation. Here, Palani meets Karthikeyan (Mammootty), who oversees the Chennai arm of the network. Karthikeyan, like Mammootty in the 1991 Thalapathi , is a gangster well-loved by his neighbourhood. He has his own codes and is mindful of who is most vulnerable to the ongoing feud between smugglers and cops. He values loyalty above all else. As Palani and Karthikeyan grow closer, OM makes some vague attempts to recall the bond between Devaraj (Mammootty) and Surya (Rajinikanth) in Thalapathi but isn’t too serious about it. Palani’s handler is Nithya Reddy (Sai Pallavi), who heads the AP task force. She has personal as well as professional reasons to stop the smuggling network. Soon, Palani makes himself Karthikeyan’s most trusted worker and surrogate son. Using this leverage, Nithya makes plans to bring in the network’s entire high command, including a mysterious boss known only as Abdul Hamid (Naseeruddin Shah). Shah is criminally wasted in his role. Even the best-laid plans need convoluted Kollywood plot twists, however. The Seshachalam extrajudicial killings, or an event closely based on it, down to the year and region, upset events on both sides. Palani, who is already battling with his affection for Karthikeyan, is left hollowed out and derailed. Suddenly, the binary of heroes and villains blurs for him. Nithya too is horrified. Yet she remains undeterred, setting up conflict between her and Palani. The first half closes with a whirlwind of moving chess pieces and complex moral questions. Despite the overly convenient twists, OM keeps you hooked until the interval. Then comes a second half that wants to do and say too much with the remaining 1 hour 30 minutes. How much can the film authentically probe police brutality? OM can’t decide. It raises pertinent questions such as asking who gets killed off in ‘encounters’ and who gets a chance to plead their case legally. But it quickly finds inane arguments to refute exactly that. The vulnerability of Adivasi communities to police overreach is highlighted and again undercut by highly sentimentalised victim blaming and saviour tropes. Any real confrontation between state authorities and the families of victims of extrajudicial killings is swiftly taken off camera. Dhanush has done all the talking required that the audiences need to listen to. What kind of political impact OM, with its Chandrababu Naidu look-alike Andhra chief minister, may achieve remains to be seen. It is appreciable that the film has brought the Seshachalam killings back into the limelight. But it also takes care to present the issue as the work of a few bad apples rather than the result of systemic police overreach. How much does such a narrative truly benefit the victims of state violence? While the second half fractalises in many directions, it is OM ’s stars who keep you caring at all. Sai Pallavi is brilliant and a constant joy to watch. She flows effortlessly between Tamil, Telugu and English dialogues, never losing momentum or gravitas. Whether faced with moral ambiguity on the job or engaged in fight sequences alongside Dhanush and Mammootty, she is flawless. Next to her, Dhanush comes across as unexceptional. His performance is solid and hard to fault. Yet, it’s barely a role that’ll stay with you like his characters in Vada Chennai (2018), Asuran (2019) or Karnan (2021). It’s really Palani’s relationship with Karthikeyan that makes his role work. Karthikeyan, while bafflingly too trusting for a crime boss, is the most human when he has to accept who Palani really is. He is hurt; he grieves. But never does he have a moment of rage at the betrayal. He meets this pain with the world-weariness of a man who has been fighting for too long. Sreeleela as Palani’s wife, Roja, is the weakest link in the cast. Too often, she is simply too grating. She comes across more as a sulky child than an adult attempting to communicate her anger and needs. OM works best during its first half, leading up to an emotional interval sequence. It just feels as if the film lost interest in itself after the break and tried to make up with increasingly handy twists and prolonged fight sequences. Listen and follow on YouTube Listen and follow on Apple Listen and follow on Spotify In this week’s South Central, hosts Dhanya Rajendran and Pooja Prasanna examine a major international investigation into Deutsche Bank. They are joined by investigative journalist Josy Joseph, who led the investigation against Deutsche Bank. The investigation is based on approximately 15.5 million internal documents. Josy explains how the documents point to Deutsche Bank’s role in enabling sanctioned oligarchs to conceal their wealth and facilitating large-scale money laundering. He describes the bank as one of the central pieces of infrastructure in the global financial system, with its operations and correspondent banking networks spanning countries across the world. The conversation explores how financial institutions are supposed to identify suspicious transactions, why red flags can be overlooked, and how the pursuit of profit can take precedence over compliance. Joseph explains how internal alerts and anti-money laundering checks can be overridden when business interests take priority. Josy also discusses some of the stories emerging from the investigation, including money-laundering schemes with Russian connections, transactions linked to the Trump family, and money routed through Deutsche Bank to Israel amid the war in Gaza. He says the team is only beginning to uncover what lies within the millions of documents, with more stories, including those connected to South Asia, still to emerge. In the second part of the episode, the hosts turn to the growing number of social media posts being taken down following government requests. In Kerala alone, 15,000 posts have been removed from social media since the UDF came to power in May 2026, according to a figure presented by a minister in the state Assembly. The conversation also discusses takedown requests reported in other states. They are joined by lawyer Nikhil Narendran, to explain how government-ordered content removals work, the legal provisions being used, and what this means for freedom of expression online. The discussion also examines the lack of transparency around takedown requests, the absence of an effective appeals process for users, and the implications for journalists, independent media and ordinary social media users. articles.summary: Close to 19 months after journalist Rejaz M Sheeba Sydeek was arrested by the Maharashtra police and charged under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act (UAPA), a Nagpur court discharged him from offences charged under the UAPA. The District and Session Court of Nagpur, which heard Rejaz’s case, posted his bail hearing for December 3. Rejaz was arrested in Nagpur on May 7, 2025, for alleged links to banned terrorist organisations. A week later, the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) took over the investigation and invoked Sections 38 (associating with listed terrorist organisations) and 39 (supporting terrorist organisation with intent of furthering its activities) of the UAPA. Rejaz has been held at the Nagpur Central Jail ever since his arrest in May 2025. He has by now spent 560 days in prison, with multiple applications for bail having previously been denied by courts. While the UAPA charges against him have been discharged, the court ordered that the charge be framed against him for offences under Sections 152 and 353 (1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). BNS 152 deals with acts endangering the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India. It replaced Section 124 A of the now repealed Indian Penal Code (IPC), which dealt with sedition. BNS 353 (1) deals with assaulting or using criminal force against a public servant. The UAPA allegations against Rejaz had centred largely on the claim by investigators that they found allegedly incriminating material on his electronic devices and during a search of his residence in Ernakulam. They alleged that he had links with members of the banned Communist Party of India (Maoist) and other banned organisations. Among the material cited by investigators were conversations on Signal and Telegram, phone numbers allegedly belonging to people associated with banned organisations, and literature concerning the CPI (Maoist), Kashmir, and armed groups. Police also claimed to have recovered several phones, pen drives, a hard drive, a memory card, and other electronic devices from his home. Investigators had also questioned Rejaz's presence in Nagpur, a city with several sensitive security installations. Police said he had travelled there to meet a woman he had met on Instagram. They also cited photographs taken at a gun shop where the woman had photographed Rejaz holding an air rifle and a pistol. Rejaz, who was 26 years old at the time of his arrest, holds a degree in social work from Kerala University, has contributed to independent platforms like Maktoob and Counter Currents. His journalism has frequently focused on police brutality, systemic discrimination, and the plight of prisoners in India.
